gaps.what: The land Goguryeo held after 468 and 489 (Gangwon edge, northern frontier of North Gyeongsang) is written as losses here with a confidence-1 regain in 551, but no page dates the regain or names the cities; goguryeo (jk-02-b) has not yet narrowed /ledger/33, drawn the land in its keyframes for 468-550 or added the 551 loss. The reach of silla_555 to the east coast (40.1 N, 7,600 km2) is on no page (Three Kingdoms of Korea, Silla and Jinheung pages silent); the 378 found event is a bridge (Naemul page silent on Jinhan).

The 905 loss of the centre and north is a confidence-1 bridge (Gungye page dates Pyongyang only, implicitly; Later Three Kingdoms page silent on Kung Ye); the 682 found event is a bridge (Sinmun page: coronation 681); the 9,400 km2 strip at 39.4-40.1 N goes to nobody in 905 at confidence 1 with no page.

goryeo_1356 adds 43,700 km2 (Chagang, Ryanggang, North Hamgyong, north South Pyongan) beyond goryeo_1290 plus Hamgyong-namdo with no page (Gongmin of Goryeo and Ssangseong Prefecture pages name only the Ssangseong and Dongnyeong provinces); the 1258 Ssangseong loss is nearly invisible (keyframes stop at 39.45 N, page gives only Kumya County); the Nine Fortresses' extent and the Goryeo-Jurchen War page are unresolved; the Gongmin page puts Dongnyeong's return in 1356, the Goryeo under Mongol rule page in 1290 (1290 kept).

Goryeo as a vassal of Liao (1022), Jin (1126..) and the Mongols/Yuan (1259 or 1270..1356), and the 1370 end of the Yuan tribute, are not ledger events here; the suzerain dossiers carry vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart goryeo. The Jin end year and the Ming relation are on no page opened. Cliopatria's Liao shape holds almost all of North Pyongan for 993-1125 (Great Jin 1130, Mongol 1260): ea-05 and ia-02 must remove it.
Not touched (reviewer verdict thin): the 705, 741 and 825 steps are confidence-1 bridges; rulers omitted.

Not touched (reviewer verdict fix): no page dates Gungye's conquests except Pyongyang (905); /ledger/5 quotes the Naju sentence loosely (Gyeon Hwon page reads 'Then in 910, when Wang Kŏn, the general of the rival kingdom of Majin, attacked and captured the city of Naju').

problems: ROUTE TO goguryeo (jk-02-b): silla now carries losses to goguryeo in 468 (same region as goguryeo /ledger/30) and 489. The 489 region differs on purpose: goguryeo /ledger/33 ({North Gyeongsang x Silla@489}, 23,267 km2, Gyeongju included) should become {intersect: [{border_band: {a: silla, b: goguryeo, year: 489, width: 3}}, {cliopatria: Silla, year: 489}, {admin1: North Gyeongsang, country: South Korea}]} (3,794 km2). goguryeo also needs keyframes drawing the 468 and 489 land until 550 and a loss to silla in 551 (silla has a confidence-1 gain from goguryeo in 551, union of both regions); until then that land is nobody's for 468-550. goguryeo dates Silla's Han valley gain to 553, silla's Han gain from goguryeo (551) now excludes Gyeonggi.

ROUTE TO taebong/colour agents: unified-silla now has a 901 loss to taebong (Kaesong 100 km, mirror of taebong /ledger/0) and its 905 loss mirrors taebong /ledger/3 and /4 (Taebong 911 outline minus the Kaesong circle, plus the Pyongyang circle's part of Unified Silla 892); 9,357 km2 at 39.4-40.1 N pass to nobody in 905.

ROUTE TO ea-05 and ia-02: goryeo /ledger/7 now names jurchens as the counterpart of the 993 gain (Goryeo-Khitan War page: the land 'was at the time occupied by Jurchen tribes'); Cliopatria's Liao shape holds 17,956 of North Pyongan's 18,209 grid km2 for 993-1125 (Great Jin 1130, Mongol Empire 1260 too) and must lose it. A jurchens dossier is still needed (1104-1108 contest, 993 gain counterpart).

Disagreement with the reviewer (unified-silla finding 3): the 11,128 km2 strip at 39.4-40.1 N was not cut from unified-silla_682/_892 and silla_676 (the Silla-Tang War page's Taedong-to-East-Korea-Bay line is not precise enough, and a cut touches silla_676 and five ledger regions); the reviewer's second option, a 905 loss to nobody, was written instead. Noted in history/polities/_notes/jk-02-c.md.

Deviation from the reviewer's wording (unified-silla finding 2): the 905 loss region is the union of (Taebong 911 minus Kaesong 100 km) and (Pyongyang 100 km within Unified Silla 892), because the Pyongyang circle reaches 7 grid cells inside the 892 outline beyond Taebong 911; with the reviewer's region alone those cells would be drawn twice.

Pages opened again in the fix round (13 distinct): Jangsu of Goguryeo, Naemul of Silla, Three Kingdoms of Korea, Silla, Jinheung of Silla, Unified Silla, Gungye, Gyeon Hwon, Later Three Kingdoms of Korea, Sinmun of Silla, Goryeo-Khitan War, Ssangseong Prefecture, Gongmin of Goryeo. The Three Kingdoms of Korea, Later Three Kingdoms, Sinmun, Ssangseong and Naemul pages were silent on the thin items they were tried for. WebFetch summaries are model-generated; quotations were taken from them verbatim.

The reviewer's Naju fix for goryeo needed no change to hubaekje or taebong (taebong_911 and hubaekje_910/926 already carry Naju as Taebong's); the gazetteer still lacks Naju and Jinju (warnings only), and the jurchens slug has no dossier (warning).

silla (378..681) and unified-silla (682..935) are one kingdom with two Cliopatria rows; taebong (901..918) and goryeo (918..1392) may be one state: the colour agent should give each pair one colour family.
